cases.purpose: Upstream differential: the markdown block grammar parses a.md to the same S-expression as the neovim-bundled upstream runtime and grammar.

files.a.md:
# Title

A paragraph with *emphasis* and `code`.

- one
- two

```sh
echo hi
```
files.parse.lua:
local f = assert(io.open(arg[1], "rb")); local text = f:read("*a"); f:close()
local lang = arg[2]
local ok, parser = pcall(vim.treesitter.get_string_parser, text, lang)
if not ok then io.stdout:write("ERR " .. tostring(parser) .. "\n") os.exit(3) end
local tree = parser:parse()[1]
io.stdout:write(tree:root():sexpr() .. "\n")
os.exit(0)

cases.oracle: Neovim 0.10.4 (Debian neovim 0.10.4-8) on the reference PATH: its built-in tree-sitter 0.22 runtime and bundled markdown / markdown_inline grammars parse the same input (vim.treesitter.get_string_parser(...):parse()[1]:root():sexpr()); the output is compared with the candidate's ts parse for the same grammar.
cases.comparison: out.txt (S-expression) and rc compared between neovim and the candidate; status of both must be 0.
cases.reference_script:
export XDG_STATE_HOME=$HOME/st XDG_CACHE_HOME=$HOME/ca XDG_DATA_HOME=$HOME/da XDG_CONFIG_HOME=$HOME/cf
/usr/bin/nvim --headless --clean -i NONE -l parse.lua a.md markdown > out.txt 2>err.txt; echo "rc=$?" > rc
cases.candidate_script: ts parse -L markdown < a.md > out.txt 2>err.txt; echo "rc=$?" > rc
